verses.1: The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.2: You must not take a wife for yourself, nor must you have sons or daughters in this place.
verses.3: For the LORD says concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, concerning their mothers who gave them life, and concerning their fathers who begot them in this land:
verses.4: They will die from plague, not mourned, not buried. They will lie like refuse on the face of the earth. They will fall by the sword and by famine. Their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and for the beasts of the earth.
verses.5: For the LORD says: Do not enter the house of mourning, nor go to lament, nor mourn for them. Because I have taken my peace away from this people, says the LORD, I have taken away their steadfast love and their compassion.
verses.6: The great and the small will die in this land. They will not be buried, nor will anyone mourn for them, nor will anyone shave their head or cut their beard for them.
verses.7: No one will hold a mourning feast for them to comfort the dead. No one will offer a cup of comfort to them for their father or mother.
verses.8: You must not go to a banquet to sit among them to eat and drink.
verses.9: For the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I will surely remove from this place, in your sight and in your days, the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of a bridegroom and the sound of a bride.
verses.10: And it will happen when you tell this people all these words, and they ask you, Why has the LORD spoken all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity, and what is our sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?
verses.11: Then you will say to them: Because your ancestors abandoned me, says the LORD, and went after other gods and served them and worshiped them, and abandoned me and did not keep my teaching.
verses.12: And you yourselves have done worse than your ancestors. You all follow the desires of your evil hearts, not listening to me.
verses.13: I will therefore remove you from this land to a land you do not know, you and your ancestors. There you will serve other gods day and night, for whom I will not show mercy.
verses.14: Therefore, the days are coming, says the LORD, when it will no longer be said, "The LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,"
verses.15: But rather, "The LORD lives, who brought up the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them." And I will return them to their land that I gave to their ancestors.
verses.16: I will send many fishermen, says the LORD, and they will fish them out. And afterward I will send many hunters and they will hunt them down on every mountain and every hill and out of the caves in the rocks.
verses.17: For my eyes are on all their ways. Their iniquities are not hidden from me.
verses.18: And I will repay their sins and their iniquities, for the defilement they have caused in my land with the corpses of their abominations and with their sins, which have filled my inheritance.
verses.19: O LORD, you are my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble. To you the nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, "Our ancestors inherited false gods, and there is no benefit in them."
verses.20: Can a man make gods for himself, and they are not gods?
verses.21: Therefore, I will surely make them know my hand and my might, and they will come to know that my name is the LORD.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 5: "I have taken my peace away from this people" — the Hebrew "שְׁלוֹמִי" is "my peace," not "their peace," reflecting the LORD's withdrawal of his peace.  
- v. 13: "whom I will not show mercy" — the Hebrew "לֹא־אֶתֵּן לָכֶם חֲנִינָה" is a direct statement that the LORD will not show mercy to them.  
- v. 19: "The LORD... the nations will come" — the reference to nations is consistent with the context of exile and the message to all peoples.  
- v. 21: "I will surely make them know" — the Hebrew "מוֹדִיעָם בַּפַּעַם הַזֹּאת" is "I will make them know in this time," translated as "I will surely make them know" to capture the immediacy.

[3] For the LORD says concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, concerning their mothers who gave them life, and concerning their fathers who begot them in this land:

[5] For the LORD says: Do not enter the house of mourning, nor go to lament, nor mourn for them. Because I have taken my peace away from this people, says the LORD, I have taken away their steadfast love and their compassion.  
[6] The great and the small will die in this land. They will not be buried, nor will anyone mourn for them, nor will anyone shave their head or cut their beard for them.  
[7] No one will hold a mourning feast for them to comfort the dead. No one will offer a cup of comfort to them for their father or mother.  
[8] You must not go to a banquet to sit among them to eat and drink.

[14] Therefore, the days are coming, says the LORD, when it will no longer be said, "The LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,"

Notes  
- v. 5: "I have taken my peace away from this people" — the Hebrew "שְׁלוֹמִי" is "my peace," not "their peace," reflecting the LORD's withdrawal of his peace.
